simple.meaning: לָעַב (lâʻab) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to deride.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in 2 Chronicles, beginning at 2 Chronicles 36:16. The surrounding contexts include prophetic witness.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to לָעַב (H3931) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: לָעַב (lâʻab) / H3931 is traced through 2 Chronicles 36:16 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H3931. laab [ לָעַב ] verb jest (Late Hebrew Hiph`il id. ; לְעַב ᵑ7 Ethpa`al id. ; Syriac Ethpa`al mock, delight oneself, be greedy ; Arabic play, sport, jest ); — only Hiph`il Participle בְּ מַלְעִבִים ׳וַיִּהְיוּ 2Chr 36:16 and they were (continually) making jest at the messengers of God.
